title: Respiratory physiology MCQ reference collection
note: Undated 72-item physiology teaching bank with five options per item and no supplied answer key. Kept outside default exam-paper selection. Source variants and defective stems are retained; validated keys are editorial checks, not official exam answers.

questions.prompt: The physiological dead space:
options: Is exactly equal to the anatomic dead space in normal people
Is measured by single breath nitrogen analysis
Is higher in elderly than young adults
Is the same as the physiological shunt
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Physiological dead space generally rises with age as matching becomes less uniform; 'exactly equal' is too absolute.

questions.prompt: A high alveolo-arterial PO2 difference most likely results from:
options: Low fractional concentration of O2 in the inspired air
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Pulmonary edema causes gas-exchange impairment and an increased A-a oxygen gradient; pure hypoventilation or low inspired oxygen alone does not.

questions.prompt: At 33 feet under water the ambient pressure is:
options: Same as the pressure in a tunnel 33 feet below sea level
Half the pressure 33 feet above sea level
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: At approximately 33 feet (10 m) of seawater, the water adds one atmosphere to the surface atmosphere, for two atmospheres absolute.

questions.prompt: Which of the following combinations are typical findings in compensated respiratory alkalosis:
options: Low PaCO2, low bicarbonate level and normal pH
Low PaCO2, normal bicarbonate level and high pH
Low PaCO2, low bicarbonate level and high pH
Low PaCO2, normal bicarbo nate level and normal pH
Low PaCO2, high bicarbonate level and high pH
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Ambiguous degree of compensation: low PaCO2 with low bicarbonate fits respiratory alkalosis, but whether pH remains high or is described as normal depends on duration and the meaning of 'compensated'. Options A and C cannot be separated safely from the supplied wording.

questions.prompt: The partial pressure of oxygen in the alveoli is expected to be least affected by:
options: Fractional concentration of O2 in ispired air
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Hemoglobin concentration changes oxygen content much more directly than alveolar oxygen partial pressure.

questions.prompt: A veno-arterial shunt is likely to:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: A right-to-left (veno-arterial) shunt introduces poorly oxygenated blood into systemic arterial blood.

questions.prompt: The arterio-venous difference of O2 is highest across:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Myocardium has high resting oxygen extraction and the largest typical arteriovenous oxygen difference among these choices.

questions.prompt: In a patient, hypoventilation is most likely if:
options: pH of arterial blood is low
O2 in arterial blood is low
PCO2 of expired air is high
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Alveolar hypoventilation raises arterial PCO2 when CO2 production is unchanged.

questions.prompt: A decrease in the recoil force of the lung is likely to:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Loss of inward elastic recoil moves the lung/chest equilibrium toward a greater FRC.

questions.prompt: Central chemoreceptors differ from chemoreceptors in that they:
options: Do not respond to changes in PO2
Become more sensitive to CO2 with chronic exposure
They are less sensitive to changes in PaCO2 than pH
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The intended comparison is central versus peripheral chemoreceptors. Central receptors have little direct hypoxic ventilatory response.

questions.prompt: Surfactant:
options: Helps to equalize pressure within interconnected alveoli
Reduces surface tension more effectively as alveolus becomes smaller
Increases the slope of the pressure-volume curve
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Surfactant stabilizes alveoli, lowers surface tension most in smaller alveoli, and increases compliance (pressure-volume slope).

questions.prompt: One month of an exposure to an inspired CO2 of 5% would result in:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Chronic hypercapnia evokes renal bicarbonate retention and buffering adaptation.

questions.prompt: In a normal adult man, breathing 100% oxygen:
options: Is likely to double O2 in arterial blood
Is likely to reduce alveolar PCO2
Is likely to raise PO2 in venous blood to about 200 mmHg
Is likely to raise arterial PO2 to about 660 mmHg
Increases the affinity of hemoglobin to oxygen
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: At sea level, breathing pure oxygen greatly raises arterial PO2 but adds relatively little hemoglobin-bound oxygen because hemoglobin is already nearly saturated.

questions.prompt: At the end of maximum inspiration:
options: Recoil force of the chest is greater than the recoil force of the lung
Average alveolar PO2 is lower than at the end of maximum expiration
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: At the end of inspiration with an open airway and no airflow, alveolar pressure equals atmospheric pressure (zero gauge).

questions.prompt: On ascent to a high altitude:
options: The concentration of oxygen in the air decreases
The number of oxygen molecules per liter of air decreases
Alveolar PCO2 is kept constant despite the high ventilation
The PCO2 in air is the same as at sea level
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Oxygen fraction stays approximately constant while barometric pressure, density and molecules per unit volume fall with altitude.

questions.prompt: Compliance of the lung:
options: Is higher in small children than in adults
Is normally twice the compliance of the chest
Is higher in elderly than young adults
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Aging reduces pulmonary elastic recoil and tends to increase static lung compliance; chest-wall compliance changes differently.

questions.prompt: Dennervation of carotid and aortic bodies leads to all the following except:
options: Decreased sensitivity of ventilation to change in PCO2
Decreased sensitivity of ventilation to change in pH
Complete absence of response of ventilation to change in PO2
Absence response of ventilation to exercise
Decreased sensitivity of ventilaton to stagnant hypoxia
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Exercise ventilation also has central command and non-chemoreceptor inputs, so peripheral chemodenervation does not abolish the response to exercise.

questions.prompt: Exchange of which of the following gases across the respiratory membrane is normally diffusion limited:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: CO binds hemoglobin avidly, maintaining a very low capillary partial pressure and diffusion-limited uptake.

questions.prompt: Minute ventilation is:
options: The volume of air moved in or out of the alveoli per minute
The volume of air moved in or out of the lung per breath
Alveolar ventilation plus dead space ventilation
Invariably increases if the respiratory rate increases
Is measured using Bohr's equation (CO2 analysis in expired air)
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Minute ventilation equals alveolar plus dead-space ventilation.

questions.prompt: The ventilatory response to hypoxia:
options: Is mediated by the central chemoreceptors
Is largely mediated by the aortic bodies in humans
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Time-dependent ambiguity: over minutes sustained hypoxia can produce a biphasic response with ventilatory decline (C), whereas over days acclimatization increases ventilation (making E plausible). The stem specifies no duration.

questions.prompt: With respect to oxygen and carbon dioxide transport in the blood:
options: For the same partial pressure a unit of blood carries the same amount of O2 and CO2
High PCO2 favors O2 binding to hemoglobin
Oxygenation of hemoglobin increases the affinit y of hemoglobin to CO 2
Per unit volume of arterial blood there is more O2 than CO2
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Metabolic acidosis normally triggers compensatory hyperventilation, lowering arterial PCO2.

questions.prompt: PCO2 in arterial blood:
options: Stimulates ventilation mainly through peripheral chemoreceptors
Is the major controller of ventilation
Increases on ascent to high altitude
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Arterial CO2 is a major chemical controller of ventilation under ordinary resting conditions.

questions.prompt: The functional residual capacity:
options: Is the volume of air in the lung at the end of normal inspiration
Is about 3 liters in an average adult male
Is about 1 liter in average adult male
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: More than one plausible true statement: FRC increases with age (B), and an approximate 3 L (D) can fit an adult male depending on body size/reference. The source supplies no key or assumptions to select uniquely.

questions.prompt: At the end of inspiration at sea level the PO2 in the anatomic dead space is approximately:
options: Above a hundred but less than 150 mmHg
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The final inspired conducting-airway gas is humidified inspired air: (760-47) x 0.21, approximately 150 mmHg.

questions.prompt: Which is true concerning control of ventilation:
options: Ventilation is more sensitive to changes in PO2 than changes in PCO2 in arterial blood
Carbon dioxide stimulates ventilation only through the central chemoreceptors
At high altitude the primary stimulus to ventilation is high PCO2
The response of ventilation to a sustained rise in PCO 2 increases wi th time
Cutting the vagus nerves decreases the depth of breathing
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: No unambiguously true option. Ventilation is strongly CO2-sensitive; CO2 acts centrally and peripherally; hypoxia drives altitude ventilation; chronic hypercapnic drive adapts downward; vagotomy tends to deepen breathing.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is likely to decrease airway resistance?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Higher lung volume provides radial traction that widens intrapulmonary airways.

questions.prompt: Compared to normal arterial blood, normal mixed venous blood has:
options: Higher PO2, lower PCO2 and higher pH
Lower PO2, higher PCO2 and higher pH
Lower PO2, higher PCO2 and lower pH
Lower PO2, lower PCO2 and higher pH
Higher PO2, lower PCO2 and lower pH
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Mixed venous blood has lower PO2, higher PCO2, and lower pH than systemic arterial blood.

questions.prompt: Deficiency of surfactant is likely to result in:
options: Reduced surface tension of fluid in the alveoli
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Surfactant deficiency raises surface tension, decreases compliance, and increases work of breathing.

questions.prompt: For a normal Hb-O2 dissociation curve, the most correct relationship is:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: A normal PO2 near 95 mmHg corresponds to approximately 97% saturation.

questions.prompt: In a normal subject, blood at the end of the pulmonary capillary:
options: Has a PO2 similar to blood in the left ventricle
Has a PO2 similar to that in the left atrium
Has a PO2 higher than blood from the aorta
Contains 20 mL of CO2 per 100 mL
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: End-pulmonary-capillary blood precedes normal venous admixture; its PO2 is slightly higher than systemic arterial blood.

questions.prompt: PCO2 in arterial blood:
options: Stimulates ventilation mainly through peripheral chemoreceptors
Is lower than normal in compensa ted metabolic acidosis
Increases on ascent to high altitude
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Compensatory hyperventilation lowers PCO2 in metabolic acidosis.

questions.prompt: In which of the following conditions is the percent saturation of hemoglobin in arterial blood likely to be normal :
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Anemia can leave arterial oxygen saturation normal while decreasing hemoglobin concentration and oxygen content.

questions.prompt: At which of the following points is the intrapleural pressure closest to zero:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Intrapleural pressure at 'maximum expiration' depends on whether expiration is forced and on the effort. The stem lacks enough maneuver detail to rank its closeness to zero against quiet end-expiration.

questions.prompt: Regarding the vital capacity, all of the following are correct except:
options: It is higher in young adults than small children
It is higher in males than females
It is normal in pure restrictive lung disease
It can be measured by simple spirometry
It is related to body size
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Vital capacity decreases in restrictive lung disease.

questions.prompt: Immediate acclimatization to high altitude is by:
options: Shift of hemoglobin dissociation curve to the left
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Several options can occur acutely at altitude: hyperventilation, increased cardiac output, and a left shift from respiratory alkalosis. Hyperventilation is the likely intended principal response, but the supplied single-answer stem is not exclusive.

questions.prompt: At the end of maximal expiration the volume of air in the lungs is:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Residual volume remains after maximal expiration; RV = TLC - VC.

questions.prompt: At the end of expiration at sea level the PO2 in the anatomic dead space is approximately:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: At end expiration, conducting airways contain alveolar gas, whose PO2 is about 100-104 mmHg.

questions.prompt: Which is true regarding lung and chest wall mechanics:
options: At maximum expiration the lungs have no tendency to collapse but the chest has a great tendency to expand
At end of normal inspiration the recoil tendency of the lung is greater than that of the chest
During inspiration the recoil tendencies of both the lungs and chest increases
At the end of normal expiration the recoil tendency of the chest is slightly greater than that of the lung
The combined compliance is greater than the individual compliances of the lung and chest
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Above FRC at the end of a normal inspiration, net respiratory-system recoil is inward; lung inward recoil exceeds chest-wall outward recoil.

questions.prompt: Which is true concerning the diffusing capacity of the lungs:
options: It increases whenever the partial pressure gradient increases
It increases as the alveolar capillary surface area rises
It increases as the thickness of the respiratory membrane area rises
It is usually measured using carbon dioxide
It is usually measured using oxygen
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Diffusing capacity increases with effective alveolar-capillary surface area; gradient changes transfer rate rather than capacity.

questions.prompt: A person whose anatomic dead space is 100 mL breathes 12 times per minute with a tidal volume of 400 mL. His pulmonary ventilation is:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Pulmonary (minute) ventilation = 400 mL x 12/min = 4.8 L/min. Alveolar ventilation would instead be 3.6 L/min.

questions.prompt: While repaying the O2 dept:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Recovery after exercise is incompletely specified. Minute ventilation generally declines toward baseline during oxygen-debt repayment, but CO2, blood flow and respiratory rate also vary with recovery phase. No supplied key identifies the intended time comparison.

questions.prompt: An average adult male has a vital capacity of:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The textbook average male VC is approximately 4.6 L; 5 L is the nearest option, not a universal predicted normal.

questions.prompt: The residual volume can be calculated by subtracting the expiratory reserve volume from:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: FRC = ERV + RV, so RV = FRC - ERV.

questions.prompt: The volume of air that describes the lung's ability to eliminate carbon dioxide is:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Effective alveolar ventilation governs CO2 elimination at a given CO2 production rate.

questions.prompt: A decrease in the recoil force of the lung is expected to:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Reduced lung recoil increases FRC by shifting the passive equilibrium volume.

questions.prompt: Deficiency of surfactant may lead to:
options: Decreased recoil force of the lung
An increase in functional residual capacity
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Surfactant deficiency increases surface tension and the inspiratory work required.

questions.prompt: Continuous measurement of the concentration of nitrogen in the expired air can be used to measure:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Method under-specified: a single-breath nitrogen curve measures anatomical dead space (C), while multiple-breath nitrogen washout measures FRC (D). 'Continuous measurement' alone does not choose a protocol.

questions.prompt: Oxygen consumption of an average adult man per minute is about:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The standard resting adult oxygen-consumption teaching value is approximately 250 mL/min.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is expected to increase function residual capacity:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Degeneration of elastic tissue reduces inward recoil and increases FRC.

questions.prompt: The most likely cause of hypoxic hypoxia together with hypercapnia is:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Hypoventilation directly combines low alveolar/arterial oxygen with retained CO2.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is correct regarding blood in the pulmonary trunk:
options: Bicarbonate concentration lower than in the aorta
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: No defensible listed value: normal pulmonary-trunk mixed venous blood is about PO2 40 mmHg, saturation 75%, PCO2 46 mmHg, and has more bicarbonate than arterial blood. Nitrogen pressure is not normally higher than aortic blood.

questions.prompt: Ventilation is most sensitive to changes in:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Within the usual physiological range, ventilation responds particularly strongly to arterial PCO2.

questions.prompt: Inspiration is initiated by discharge from:
options: The dorsal inspiratory group of neurons
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Ambiguous distinction: the pre-Botzinger complex participates in rhythm generation (C), while dorsal inspiratory neurons provide an inspiratory ramp (A). 'Initiated by discharge' does not distinguish rhythm generation from the older teaching account of inspiratory output.

questions.prompt: Voluntary hyperventilation by a normal person is expected to lead to all the following except:
options: Low blood bicarbonate concentration in arterial blood
A great increase in oxygen concentration in arterial blood
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Hemoglobin is already nearly saturated, so voluntary hyperventilation does not greatly increase arterial oxygen content.

questions.prompt: The normal diffusing capacity of the respiratory membrane of an average adult male for oxygen is about:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The conventional resting oxygen diffusing capacity is about 21 mL/min/mmHg, so 25 is nearest. The source incorrectly abbreviates the units to 'ml'; these are not standalone volumes.

questions.prompt: Cyanosis is unlikely to occur in:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Severe anemia may prevent accumulation of enough deoxygenated hemoglobin for visible cyanosis despite hypoxia. Radiation and convection are anomalous distractors retained from the source.

questions.prompt: Which is true concerning the diffusing capacity of the lungs:
options: Rises as the partial pressure gradient rises
Rises as the effective surface area of the respiratory membrane rises
Is not affected by the thickness of the respiratory membrane
Is not affected by the diffusion coefficient of the membrane to gases
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Increasing effective gas-exchange surface area increases diffusing capacity.

questions.prompt: Which type of hypoxia in which there is a greater than normal atrial-mixed venous partial pressure difference and relatively normal arterial oxygen concentration:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Low tissue blood flow increases extraction and the arterial-mixed venous oxygen difference while arterial oxygen can remain normal. 'atrial' appears to mean arterial.

questions.prompt: Administration of a gas mixture with higher than normal oxygen concentration at atmospheric pressure would elevate hypoxia due to:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Unscored because the source literally says 'elevate hypoxia'. B (diffusion impairment) would be the intended answer if 'elevate' were corrected to 'alleviate', but that correction reverses the stem's meaning. The original wording and options are preserved without assigning a validated key to the malformed question.

questions.prompt: The PCO2 is an alveolus which is ventilated but not perfused is about:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: An unperfused but ventilated alveolus approaches inspired gas; its PCO2 is approximately atmospheric (0.3 mmHg in the source's teaching approximation).

questions.prompt: Which is true concerning surface tension in lungs?
options: The normal amount of surfactant reduces surface tension in healthy lungs to a neglible level
In the absence of surfavtant alveoli with small radii collapse into alveoli with big radii
Surfactant is maximally concentrated at liquid-air interface at the end of inspiration
In normal lungs surface tension is responsible for 20% of the recoil force of the lung
Surface tension remains the same throughout the breathing cycle
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: With equal unopposed surface tension, Laplace pressure is greater in smaller alveoli, which tend to empty into larger ones.

questions.prompt: Which is true concerning oxygen transport in the blood?
options: If PO2 is 60 mmHg oxygen concentration is about 18 ml/100 ml blood
The P50 is the percent saturation of hemoglobin with oxygen when PO2 is 50 mmHg
The normal P50 of arterial blood is higher than that of venous blood
Increase in pH increases the P50
P50 reflects the capacity of blood to carry oxygen
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: At PO2 about 60 mmHg, saturation is around 90%, giving about 18 mL O2/100 mL at ordinary hemoglobin concentration.

questions.prompt: The physiological shunt:
options: Is equal to the physiological dead space
Is measured by single breath nitrogen analysis
Occurs only in people with respiratory diseases
Is about 5% of the cardiac output
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: No unique single answer: A correctly describes physiological shunt as wasted perfusion, while E is also a defensible approximate normal value. Official respiratory-physiology teaching material describes physiological shunt as around 5% of cardiac output. The unqualified stem does not distinguish the general definition from its normal magnitude, so it is retained unscored.

questions.prompt: At the summit of a mountain the barometric pressure was found to be 300 mmHg. The partial pressure of O2 in the air is saturated with water vapour at 37oC at this altitude is expected to be about:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Humidified inspired PO2 = (300 - 47) x 0.21 = 53.1 mmHg, nearest 55.

questions.prompt: Which of the following parameters is lower in the elderly than in young adults?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Vital capacity decreases with aging as residual volume rises.

questions.prompt: Surfactant:
options: Is produced by type I pneumocytes
Production starts only after birth in full term babies
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Surfactant deficiency lowers lung compliance; surfactant is made by type II cells before birth.

questions.prompt: At the end of normal exporation all the following are correct except:
options: Recoil tendency of the lung as acting inward to collapse the lung
Chest recoil is acting outward to expand the lung
Alveolar pressure is greater than mouth pressure
The average intrapleural pressure is zero
Surface tension is less than at the end of normal inspiration
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: There are two incorrect options at a normal no-flow end-expiratory point: alveolar pressure equals mouth pressure (so C is false), and intrapleural pressure remains negative rather than zero (so D is false).

questions.prompt: Obstructive lung disease is typically characterized by:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Airflow obstruction characteristically reduces FEV1 and FEV1/FVC.

questions.prompt: The following parameters are higher in the elderly than young adults:
options: Basal oxygen consumption per kg body weight
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Both FRC and anatomical dead space can increase with age. The question provides no single-best qualifier that resolves C versus D.

questions.prompt: The approximate dead space of a normal adult man breathing through a tube that is 50 cm long and 6mm in diameter is:
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The supplied tube is 50 cm long and 6 mm in diameter: its added volume is pi x (0.3 cm)^2 x 50 = 14.1 mL. Adding a conventional 150 mL anatomical dead space gives about 164 mL, absent from the options. Do not silently reinterpret 6 mm as 6 cm.

questions.prompt: Spontaneous respiration ceases after:
options: Transection of the spinal cord below C5
Transection of the brain stem between the pons and medulla combined with bilateral vagotomy
Complete destruction of the peripheral chemoreceptors
Transection of the spinal cord at the first cervical segment
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: E (C1 transection) removes descending drive to the phrenic motor neurons, but C merely says spinal-cord transection without a level. Because C can include the same lesion, the single-answer options overlap.

questions.prompt: All the following are expected to decrease airway resistance except:
options: Shifting from nose to mouth breathing
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Parasympathetic stimulation constricts airways; atropine and adrenergic stimulation favor lower resistance.

notes: All 10 pages and all 72 numbered items preserved. Original print is text-native and was visually reviewed for document structure and absence of a supplied key.

Similar questions are retained as variants: Q9/Q45 (reordered options), Q22/Q31 (different C statement), Q39/Q57 (different distractors), Q28/Q46 (different stem direction), Q24/Q37 (inspiration versus expiration).
Ambiguous, malformed or multiple-answer items carry null validated keys and explanatory notes.
